title: finding(scripts): `check-readme-exports.mjs --list` crashes with a TypeError on exactly the unbuilt tree its own failure message tells you to inspect
body:
Surfaced while implementing objectui#8674 (dev seat, session `session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ`), reaching for `--list` to see whether a newly added README snippet's import was judged. ⛔ Unassigned; grading and `domain:*` are triage's. ⛔ Not fixed there — a gate-tooling defect is not that card's scope.

## Measured, on `b775500af`, with a named repro

One package unbuilt is enough. Park a single `dist` that a README documents a TYPE from:

```bash
mv packages/plugin-kanban/dist /tmp/parked
node scripts/check-readme-exports.mjs --list   # crashes
node scripts/check-readme-exports.mjs          # the control: reports cleanly
mv /tmp/parked packages/plugin-kanban/dist
```

The `--list` run prints rows until it reaches the first unjudgeable documented type, then dies:

```
partial-marker     packages/plugin-gantt/README.md:423  interface GanttTask  doc 14 key(s) ...
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')
    at .../scripts/check-readme-exports.mjs:1481
```

The line it dies on formats a documented-type row and reads `t.fabricated.length` unconditionally; an unjudgeable entry (`its type entry ./dist/index.d.ts is not on disk`) reaches that formatter without the key. Stated as measured — the repair direction is the maintainer's call, not asserted here.

## The lit control, on the same tree in the same minute

The same script WITHOUT `--list` handles that state exactly as designed: a full census line, `2 unjudgeable`, and the written paragraph explaining that an unjudgeable entry is a FAILURE and not a skip. So the tree is not the problem and the gate's judgement is not the problem — only the `--list` reporting path is.

On a fully built tree `--list` exits 0 and prints all 535 judged self-imports, which is how the two states were told apart rather than guessed.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a shrug

`--list` is the script's own documented diagnostic (`node scripts/check-readme-exports.mjs --list  # every self-binding judged`, in its usage block), and the only state a developer reaches for it in is the state where the gate just failed. The plain run's failure text says `run pnpm build first`; the person who instead asks *which* bindings were judged gets a stack trace with no census, no rows past the first bad one, and nothing naming the precondition. The sibling gate `check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` answers the same state with an explicit `PRECONDITION NOT MET (exit 2)` and a scoped build command, which is the contrast that makes this look like an oversight rather than a policy.

A crash is also indistinguishable at the exit code from the fabricated-name failure the gate exists to catch: both leave `--list` at a non-zero exit.

## Scope of the duplicate search behind this filing

Bounded, and said so rather than implied: the 300 most recent rows of the repo-scoped REST issues list in **all** states (3 pages of 100) were read, of which 144 are issues and not pull requests, covering numbers **8919–9218**. Titles were scanned for `readme-exports` / `check-readme` / `--list` — zero hits, with lit controls on the same rows (`designer` matched 2, `grid` matched 7). Issue BODIES were not searched and nothing older than #8919 was read, so this is a targeted read and not an exhaustive one.
